wikirealms-legend-ceiling-note: These compare sections within one article. A poorly sourced article stays dry throughout, however uneven it is — the greens are only available to an article that cites well overall.
wikirealms-legend-range-label: A mountain range is a section
wikirealms-legend-range-detail: Its height comes from that section’s own prose, and its breadth from everything nested beneath it.
wikirealms-legend-portal-label: A portal is an outbound link
wikirealms-legend-portal-detail: Up to $1 across a world, and at most $2 per mountain range (lead links have their own small budget). They are spread across the sections rather than taken from the top, and placed in the range whose section links there. Taking one starts a new world.
wikirealms-legend-water-detail: A short article floods; a long, detailed one drains and shows more land.
wikirealms-legend-snow-label: Rock and snow are how much was written
wikirealms-legend-snow-detail: A section's own prose is what raises its peak. Stone starts showing through at $1 of the world's height and has covered the ground by $2; snow begins at $3. Both come on gradually, and they tint rather than replace: a well-sourced section's high ground is damp, mossy stone where a barren one's is dry scree, and its trees climb higher before giving out. The polar ice is the exception — every world has it.
wikirealms-legend-foliage-label: Trees and grass grow from how well a section cites
wikirealms-legend-foliage-detail: Greener ground hosts denser understory and canopy. Altitude thins them toward the treeline; barren bands stay bare. The same lushness that paints the ground is what decides how much grows on it.
wikirealms-legend-creatures-label: Fish in the seas show how many people read the article
wikirealms-legend-creatures-detail: Thirty-day pageviews fill the oceans with fish: quieter pages stay sparse, busier ones host denser schools. Wikipedia categories tint which species appear (reef fish nearer the shelf, larger ones in deeper water). Land stays clear of animals.

wikirealms-postcard-tagline-1: Every Wikipedia article is a world.
wikirealms-postcard-letter-mission: Every Wikipedia article is a world — explore knowledge as landscape, then grow the map on Wikipedia itself.
wikirealms-info-start-lead: WikiRealms turns a Wikipedia article into a place you can explore.
wikirealms-info-start-peaks: Peaks are sections. Taller means more of that section's own text; broader means a larger subsection tree.
wikirealms-info-start-water: Water rises on short articles and falls as the article grows — stubs flood; detailed pages expose more land.
wikirealms-info-start-fish: Fish are pageviews. Quieter articles stay sparse; heavily read ones fill the seas (hover a fish to see the count).
wikirealms-info-start-portals: Portals are outbound Wikipedia links. Step through one to travel to another article's world.
wikirealms-info-start-trail: Your trail remembers the path you walked. Open it from the top bar; share a realm or the whole trail from Share.
wikirealms-info-start-callout: Open Legend beside the view controls (or press L) to see what the colours and markers mean.
wikirealms-info-journey-lead: Every portal you take is kept on your trail — a map of the part of Wikipedia you have walked.
wikirealms-info-journey-back: Use back and forward (or the arrow keys) to retrace steps without losing the branch you came from.
wikirealms-info-journey-open: Open Your trail in the top bar to jump to any stop you have already visited.
wikirealms-info-journey-share: Share this realm sends a link to the world underfoot. Share my trail makes a postcard of the path.
wikirealms-info-how-lead: Each world is generated from the article's outline, prose length, and citations — the same article always produces the same place.
wikirealms-info-how-outline: Read the outline: the section tree becomes nested peaks. Top-level sections are separate mountain systems.
wikirealms-info-how-scale: Scale the terrain: a section's own prose sets peak height; its full subtree sets how broad the range is.
wikirealms-info-how-detail: Add natural detail: seeded noise roughens the structure so the map looks organic without changing between visits.
wikirealms-info-how-sea: Set sea level: total article length shifts the waterline. Stubs sit lower under water; detailed articles expose more land.
wikirealms-info-how-ground: Paint the ground: above the shore, citation density vs the article's own rate decides bare dunes through closed canopy.
wikirealms-info-how-weather: Weather the heights: rock and snow layer over high ground on top of that colour, so well-sourced peaks read damp and mossy.
wikirealms-info-how-portals: Portals from a section sit in that section's top-level range. Repeated links in one section combine; the same destination can appear in different ranges.
wikirealms-info-about-by: Created by Moriel Schottlender — an experiment in seeing knowledge networks as places.
wikirealms-info-about-pitch: What would a Wikipedia article look like as a landscape you could walk? Barren slopes and flooded maps are invitations to grow the public record; citations and prose still live on Wikipedia.
wikirealms-info-about-credits-body: Fish models from the $1 by $2 (CC0). Portal fountains use $3 by $4 (CC0).
